items.name: Badge
items.description: Pure-CSS badge: 7 variants (soft or solid tints), animatable status dot, icon, remove button, pill/square, 3 sizes, and a counter positioned on the corner of an avatar or icon.
useWhen: A short status label must sit next to an item, such as Paid, Failed or Beta
An unread count or presence dot must be pinned to the corner of an icon or avatar
Removable tags or active filters need a compact chip with a remove button

avoidWhen.when: The item is a primary action the user is expected to click
The status would be conveyed by color alone without a readable label

classes.name: mv-badge
classes.description: On <span>, or <a>/<button> for an interactive badge (hover + focus).

classes.name: mv-badge-dot
classes.description: Status dot; takes the variant’s tint or --mv-badge-dot. data-pulse: “live” ripple.

classes.name: mv-badge-remove
classes.description: Remove <button> inside the badge (the removal itself is up to you).

classes.name: mv-badge-anchor
classes.description: Relative container around an avatar/icon to place a .mv-badge[data-position] on it.

attributes.name: data-variant
attributes.type: secondary | outline | success | warning | danger | info
attributes.description: Visual style; semantic variants are tinted.

attributes.name: data-appearance
attributes.description: Semantic variant in solid color (counters, strong statuses).

attributes.name: data-shape
attributes.description: Corner shape.

attributes.name: data-size
attributes.description: Height 18 / 22 / 26px.

attributes.name: data-position
attributes.description: Counter positioned on the corner of the parent .mv-badge-anchor, cut out by a ring; empty = plain dot (unread, presence).

cssVars.description: Inward offset of the positioned badge (useful on a round avatar).

cssVars.name: --mv-badge-ring
cssVars.description: Color of the positioned badge’s cut-out ring (set it to the background color).

items.a11y: A badge is text: it’s read as is. Don’t convey information through color alone (keep a label: “Paid”, “Failed”). Positioned counter: mark it aria-hidden="true" and carry the information in the trigger’s accessible name (aria-label="Notifications, 3 unread"). Remove button: explicit aria-label (“Remove Design”) and move focus to the neighboring badge after removal. The data-pulse ripple is disabled with reduced motion.

items.name: Button
items.description: Pure-CSS button on <button> or <a>: 6 variants, 4 sizes, loading state, group.
useWhen: A form submission or in-page action needs a clear, consistently styled trigger
Actions must be ranked by importance with primary, secondary, outline, ghost, destructive or link styles
An action runs asynchronously and should show a loading state that blocks repeat clicks
Related actions should be joined into a single attached group

items.a11y: Use a real <button> (or <a href> for navigation). Icon buttons must have an aria-label.

data-size.label: Size
data-size.help: Smaller, larger, or a square icon button

aria-busy.label: Loading
aria-busy.help: Type true to show a spinner and block clicks

items.name: Checkbox
items.description: Native pure-CSS checkbox: a self-drawing (reversible) check mark, indeterminate state, sizes, invalid; also provides the shared .mv-choice and .mv-choice-card layouts (option cards highlighted via :has(:checked)).
useWhen: Users pick any number of options from a list, or give a single opt-in such as accepting terms
A select-all control needs an indeterminate state above a nested list of options
Options need richer presentation as clickable cards with a title, description and icon

avoidWhen.when: The setting takes effect immediately, like turning a feature on or off
Only one option in the set may be chosen

classes.name: mv-choice
classes.description: Shared (radio, switch): a <label> row with control + label, the control centered on the first line.

classes.name: mv-choice-card

classes.name: mv-choice-text / -title / -description

classes.name: mv-choice-icon
classes.description: Optional icon tile inside a card (tinted when checked).

classes.name: mv-choice-group
classes.description: List of options (ideally <fieldset> + <legend>).

classes.name: mv-choice-group-nested
classes.description: Indented sub-list (“select all” tree).

attributes.name: data-size

attributes.name: data-shape
attributes.description: Round box.

attributes.description: On .mv-choice-group: auto-fit grid of cards (min width --mv-choice-min).

items.a11y: Native input: role, checked/mixed state (aria-checked=mixed for indeterminate), Space and form submission handled by the browser. The wrapping <label> provides the accessible name; link the description with aria-describedby. Focus ring visible for keyboard only; animations disabled with reduced motion.

data-shape.help: Type round for a round box instead of a square

aria-invalid.label: Error state
aria-invalid.help: Type true to show a red error border

data-layout.help: Type grid to lay option cards out in a grid that fits the width

items.name: Input
items.description: Pure-CSS text field: 3 sizes, invalid (aria-invalid / :user-invalid), read-only and file states, plus a group with icons, prefixes/suffixes, inline buttons and a clear button.
useWhen: A single-line value is needed, such as a name, email, password, URL or search query
The field needs a prefix, suffix, icon, inline button or clear button inside one bordered group
Server-side or native validation errors must be shown directly on the field

avoidWhen.when: The text can span several lines, such as a comment or message

classes.name: mv-input
classes.description: On <input> (text, email, search, password, number, file…).

classes.name: mv-input-group
classes.description: Container that carries the border and focus ring; the inner .mv-input becomes borderless.

classes.name: mv-input-group-addon
classes.description: Icon, text (“https://”, “$”), <kbd> or indicator placed before/after the input. Use a <label for> so clicking it focuses the input.

classes.name: mv-input-clear
classes.description: Clear button: hidden automatically while the input is empty (the input needs a placeholder). The clearing itself is up to you (3 lines of JS).

attributes.name: data-size
attributes.description: Height 32 / 36 / 44px; on .mv-input or .mv-input-group.

attributes.name: aria-invalid
attributes.description: Forces the error state (server-side validation). :user-invalid is also supported natively.

attributes.name: data-variant (addon)

attributes.name: type="search"
attributes.description: The native clear button (WebKit/Blink) is restyled: clearing without JS.

items.a11y: Always pair with a <label for> (or aria-label). Decorative icons have aria-hidden="true". Text addons in a <label for> join the accessible name (“https://” is then announced). Inline buttons are real <button type="button"> elements with an aria-label; the show/hide password button uses aria-pressed. On error, set aria-invalid="true" and link the message via aria-describedby (see Field).

builder.summary: Text field with icons, prefixes, clear button

aria-invalid.label: Error state
aria-invalid.help: Type true to show the field in red, for example after a server check

items.name: Kbd
items.description: Subtly raised keyboard keys on <kbd>: nested combinations, 3 sizes, a flat variant, adapts inside buttons and tooltips.
useWhen: Keyboard shortcuts must be displayed in docs, menus, tooltips or a command palette
A key combination such as Ctrl+K needs to read as a group of keycaps

avoidWhen.when: The text is a status or category label rather than a key to press
The content is inline code or a command to run rather than a keyboard key

classes.name: mv-kbd
classes.description: Key, on <kbd>.

classes.name: mv-kbd-group
classes.description: Combination: a parent <kbd> holding several .mv-kbd; text between keys (“+”, “then”) stays subtle.

attributes.name: data-size
attributes.description: Height 16 / 20 / 28 px.

attributes.name: data-variant
attributes.description: No relief, tinted background (menus, command palettes).

items.a11y: Use the <kbd> element (“keyboard input” semantics). For a combination, nest the <kbd>s inside a parent <kbd>, as the HTML spec recommends. Symbols (⌘, ⇧, ⌥) are read inconsistently: add an aria-label on the group (e.g. aria-label="Command K") or a .mv-sr-only text if the shortcut is important information.

builder.summary: Keyboard shortcuts shown as keycaps

data-variant.label: Style
data-variant.help: Type flat for a tinted key without relief

items.name: Radio
items.description: Pure-CSS native radio button: an inner dot that springs in, sizes, an outline variant, inline or stacked groups, and option cards (plan lists, tiles with a badge).
useWhen: Users must choose exactly one option from a small set and benefit from seeing every choice at once
Plans or shipping methods must be compared as option cards with a price, description or badge

avoidWhen.when: There are many options and vertical space is limited
Several options can be selected at the same time

classes.name: mv-radio
classes.description: On <input type="radio">.

classes.name: mv-choice / mv-choice-card / mv-choice-group
classes.description: Shared layouts, provided by the checkbox component (dependency).

classes.name: mv-radio-meta
classes.description: Price or info aligned at the end of the card (<small> for the unit).

attributes.name: data-variant
attributes.description: On the input: neutral ring, only the dot takes the accent.

attributes.name: aria-invalid
attributes.description: Error border and halo.

attributes.name: data-variant="badge"
attributes.description: Vertical tile; the radio becomes a corner badge, visible once checked or on focus.

items.a11y: Native radios grouped by name: arrows change the option, Tab enters/leaves the group, all handled by the browser. Wrap them in <fieldset> + <legend> (or role="radiogroup" + aria-label). In the badge variant, the radio stays present and focusable (only visually hidden until checked).

builder.summary: Pick one option, as dots or cards

aria-invalid.label: Error state
aria-invalid.help: Shows a red border to flag a wrong or missing choice

items.name: Select
items.description: Styled native <select> (token-colored chevron), progressively enhanced into a customizable select (appearance: base-select): animated list, status dots, icons, descriptions and checkmark, optional “liquid” opening; clean fallback elsewhere.
useWhen: Users pick one value from a medium-sized list where native mobile pickers and keyboard support matter
Options benefit from status dots, icons or descriptions while staying a real form control
A playful liquid opening fits the product, with a clean native fallback on unsupported browsers

avoidWhen.when: The list holds actions to run rather than a value to submit
Only two to five options exist and showing them all helps the decision

classes.name: mv-select
classes.description: On <select>. Classic everywhere; customizable where appearance: base-select is supported.

classes.name: mv-select-dot
classes.description: Status dot inside an option; data-tone="success | warning | danger | info" or --mv-select-dot.

classes.name: mv-select-icon
classes.description: Option icon (svg).

classes.name: mv-select-text
classes.description: Label + description container inside an option.

classes.name: mv-select-description
classes.description: Secondary option text, hidden in the displayed value (selectedcontent).

attributes.name: data-size
attributes.description: Height 32 / 36 / 44px.

attributes.name: data-native
attributes.description: Keeps native rendering even when base-select is available.

attributes.name: aria-invalid
attributes.description: Error state; :user-invalid is supported too.

attributes.name: <button><selectedcontent>
attributes.description: Optional first child: the displayed value mirrors the selected option’s rich content (dot, icon).

attributes.name: data-open
attributes.description: Opt-in, pure CSS: the list stretches out of the trigger (a drop hanging from a neck, clip-path shape() driven by @property properties), spreads out, then pinches back into the trigger on close. Requires base-select + shape(); otherwise a standard animation. Instant with reduced motion.

items.a11y: Stays a real <select>: combobox/listbox role, keyboard (arrows, type-ahead, Enter, Escape), screen readers and native mobile pickers handled by the browser. Pair it with a <label for>. Option icons are aria-hidden. Fallback: without base-select, rich option content is reduced to its text (keep descriptions short; don’t use the label attribute, which would hide the rich content). For a required choice, use required + a first option with value="" disabled (placeholder styling applied). Known limits: the custom picker, rich options and data-open="liquid" need appearance: base-select (Chromium-based browsers today), and the liquid opening also needs clip-path: shape(); elsewhere the field stays a styled native select with plain-text options and the browser's own list.

aria-invalid.label: Error state
aria-invalid.help: Shows a red border to flag a wrong or missing choice

data-open.label: Liquid opening
data-open.help: The list flows out of the field like a drop

items.name: Separator
items.description: Pure-CSS horizontal or vertical separator: solid, dashed, dotted or faded, with a centered (“or”) or aligned label, on <hr> or <div>.
useWhen: Two groups of content or controls need a quiet visual split, horizontal or vertical
Alternative paths need a labeled divider, such as “or” between social login and email
A feed or timeline needs inline labels like Today between groups of items

avoidWhen.when: Spacing alone already separates the groups clearly and extra lines would add clutter
Sections need collapsible headings rather than a static line

classes.name: mv-separator
classes.description: On <hr> (horizontal) or <div>. If the element contains text or an icon, it becomes a labeled divider (line, label, line). Without a label, it must be strictly empty (no whitespace).

items.a11y: <hr> already has role=separator. For a semantic <div>: role="separator" + aria-orientation="vertical" when vertical. Purely decorative: role="none" (or aria-hidden="true"). With a label (“or”, “Today”), don’t set role=separator (its children would become presentational): keep a plain <div> so the text is read.

builder.summary: Divider line, plain, dashed or with a label

data-orientation.label: Vertical

data-variant.label: Line style
data-variant.help: Dashed, dotted, or fading out at both ends

data-align.help: Puts the label at the start or the end instead of the middle

items.name: Switch
items.description: Pure-CSS switch on <input type="checkbox" role="switch">: thumb that slides on a spring and stretches when pressed, icons in the thumb (customizable), sizes, label on the left or right, option card.
useWhen: A setting turns on or off and takes effect immediately, as in a preferences panel
A list of settings needs on/off rows or option cards with descriptions

avoidWhen.when: The choice only applies after submitting a form, or is an agreement such as accepting terms

classes.name: mv-switch
classes.description: On <input type="checkbox" role="switch">.

classes.name: mv-choice / mv-choice-card

attributes.name: aria-invalid

items.a11y: role="switch" on a native checkbox: state announced as “on / off”, Space toggles, value submitted with the form. The wrapping <label> provides the name; link a description via aria-describedby if needed. Icons are decorative (pseudo-elements).

data-shape.label: Square shape
data-shape.help: Slightly rounded corners instead of a pill

data-icons.label: Icons

aria-invalid.label: Error
aria-invalid.help: Shows it in the error state

items.name: Textarea
items.description: Textarea that grows on its own (field-sizing: content) between a minimum and maximum number of rows, with an optional resize handle, a group with a toolbar and an <mv-char-count> character counter.
useWhen: Users write multi-line text such as a comment, message, bio or description
The field should grow with its content between a minimum and a maximum number of rows
A character limit must be shown with a counter that warns near the limit
A composer needs a toolbar for formatting or attachment buttons next to the text

avoidWhen.when: The value is short and single-line, like a name or an email
Rich text such as headings, bold and links must render while typing; this field is plain text

classes.name: mv-textarea-toolbar-spacer
classes.description: Pushes the following items to the right.

attributes.name: <mv-char-count for>
attributes.description: Tracked control (otherwise: the first textarea/input of the parent .mv-field or group).

attributes.description: Limit. Without maxlength it is a soft limit: the control becomes invalid past it.

attributes.description: Ratio at which data-state="near" applies.

attributes.name: <mv-char-count data-variant>
attributes.description: Circular gauge; the number only appears near the limit.

methods.description: Recomputes after a programmatic value change.

items.a11y: Pair with a <label for>. <mv-char-count> adds its description (“120 characters left of 200”) to the control's aria-describedby without overwriting existing ids, and only announces (role=status) when crossing the warning threshold or the limit, not on every keystroke. The visible number is aria-hidden. Toolbar buttons are <button type="button"> with an aria-label.

builder.summary: Multi-line field that grows as you type

data-resize.label: Resize handle
data-resize.help: Lets visitors drag to resize the field

data-autosize.label: No auto grow
data-autosize.help: Keeps a fixed height instead of growing while typing

aria-invalid.label: Error
aria-invalid.help: Shows it in the error state

items.name: Field
items.description: Pure-CSS field layout: label (required / optional), help text, an error message that shows up on its own when the control is invalid, vertical, horizontal, responsive and inline orientations, choice cards and fieldset.
useWhen: Every form control needs a consistent label, help text and an error message that appears on invalid input
Settings forms should show labels on the left on wide screens and stack them on narrow ones
Related radios or checkboxes must be grouped under a legend, optionally as selectable choice cards

avoidWhen.when: The need is the text control itself rather than its label and messages

classes.name: mv-field
classes.description: Field container: label, control, description, error.

classes.name: mv-label
classes.description: Label (<label for>). Can be used on its own, outside .mv-field.

classes.name: mv-field-header
classes.description: Row with the label + a secondary element on the right (“Forgot password?” link, counter).

classes.name: mv-field-label-group
classes.description: Label + description stacked in the left column (horizontal orientation).

classes.name: mv-field-description
classes.description: Help text.

classes.name: mv-field-error
classes.description: Error message: hidden, then shown (fade) when the field contains a :user-invalid or aria-invalid="true" control, or has data-invalid. Never shown when empty.

classes.name: mv-field-group
classes.description: Stack of spaced fields; container-query container (responsive orientation).

classes.name: mv-field-row
classes.description: Side-by-side fields that wrap below 12rem.

classes.name: mv-fieldset
classes.description: On <fieldset>: styled <legend> (no notch), description, footer.

classes.name: mv-fieldset-description / -footer
classes.description: Text under the legend; action row (muted background in the card variant).

attributes.name: data-required (label)
attributes.description: Decorative asterisk (ignored by screen readers: put required on the control).

attributes.name: data-optional (label)
attributes.description: Note shown after the label, e.g. data-optional="optional".

attributes.name: data-orientation
attributes.description: horizontal: label on the left; responsive: horizontal when the container is ≥ 36rem; inline: checkbox/radio first, label next to it.

attributes.name: data-variant (field)
attributes.description: Selectable choice card (with inline orientation, on a <label>).

attributes.name: data-variant (fieldset)
attributes.description: Framed fieldset with a built-in action footer.

attributes.name: data-invalid / data-disabled
attributes.description: Forces the state on the field (otherwise inferred from the control).

cssVars.name: --mv-field-label-width
cssVars.description: Width of the label column (horizontal / responsive).

items.a11y: Associate each label with <label for="id">. Link help text and error to the control: aria-describedby="help-id error-id" (an error hidden with display:none is not read; it is as soon as it shows). Set aria-invalid="true" on the control for a server error, and required for a required field (the asterisk is decorative). Group related options in <fieldset class="mv-fieldset"> + <legend>; a disabled fieldset disables all its content. Choice cards: the <label> wraps the radio/checkbox input, and keyboard focus is shown on the card. A disabled field dims its label but keeps its help text readable (fg-subtle), since it often says why the field is locked. Forced colors: the error keeps its icon; the red tint of the label and border is lost there, so the error text itself must carry the message.

builder.summary: Label, help text and automatic error message

data-orientation.label: Label position
data-orientation.help: Label above, beside, or next to a checkbox

items.name: Dialog
items.description: Animated native <dialog> modal; also covers Alert Dialog (persistent), Sheet (4 sides) and a mobile Drawer with swipe to close.
useWhen: A blocking confirmation is needed before a destructive or irreversible action
A short form or detail view must stay in context without leaving the page
A side sheet must slide in from an edge for settings, filters or a cart
A detail panel must stay open beside a board or list that remains usable (modeless)
On mobile, a bottom drawer the user can swipe away fits better than a centered modal

avoidWhen.when: The message is transient feedback that shouldn't interrupt the user
The content is a small panel anchored to a trigger that shouldn't block the page
The flow has many steps or needs its own URL; use a dedicated page instead

attributes.name: open
attributes.description: Opens/closes the modal.

attributes.name: persistent
attributes.description: Alert mode: no closing via Escape or outside click, role=alertdialog (follows later changes).

attributes.name: swipe
attributes.description: Swipe to close (sheets / drawers); can be turned on or off at any time.

attributes.name: modeless
attributes.description: Non-modal: no backdrop, no scroll lock, the page stays usable (a side panel next to a board or a list). Escape from inside closes it (unless persistent) and focus returns to the trigger. Applies at the next opening.

methods.name: show()
methods.description: Opens as a modal (or non-modal with modeless).

events.name: mv-close
events.description: detail.returnValue: value of the [data-mv-close] button, or “dismiss” / “swipe”.

slots.name: [data-mv-open]
slots.description: Internal trigger; for an external one: data-mv-open="#id".

slots.name: <dialog>
slots.description: Content; data-variant="sheet" + data-side="right|left|top|bottom". May be rendered or replaced after the element connects (Angular, a late v-if): it is looked up when needed, and a pending open applies once it exists.

classes.name: mv-dialog-header / -title / -description / -footer / -close
classes.description: Content layout.

cssVars.name: --mv-dialog-z
cssVars.description: Stacking of a modeless dialog (a modal one sits in the top layer).

items.a11y: Focus trapped and restored by the native <dialog>, inert page, Escape. With modeless, the page is not inert and focus is not trapped (Tab can leave the panel, as for any non-modal dialog); Escape inside it closes it and focus returns to the trigger. aria-labelledby/-describedby wired automatically from .mv-dialog-title / .mv-dialog-description, checked again at each opening so a title rendered late by a framework is still used.

builder.summary: Modal, side sheet or swipeable mobile drawer

persistent.label: Must answer
persistent.help: Cannot be closed with Escape or a click outside

swipe.label: Swipe to close
swipe.help: Lets people close the panel with a swipe

modeless.label: Page stays usable
modeless.help: No backdrop: people can keep using the page beside the window

items.name: Menu
items.description: Full-featured dropdown menu: checkboxes, radio items, submenus with a safe-triangle, shortcuts, typeahead and APG keyboard navigation; opt-in data-motion="glide" (opens from the trigger’s corner, a single highlight that glides between items, submenus that slide in).
useWhen: A button opens a list of actions, such as a row's Edit, Duplicate and Delete
Actions need checkable items, radio groups, shortcuts or nested submenus
An account or overflow menu must open from a trigger with full keyboard and typeahead support

avoidWhen.when: The user is choosing a value to submit with a form
The panel holds a form or rich interactive content rather than a list of actions

attributes.name: placement
attributes.description: Panel position relative to the trigger (automatic flip/shift).

attributes.name: offset
attributes.description: Distance from the trigger (px).

attributes.name: open
attributes.description: Opens/closes programmatically (reflects the state).

attributes.name: data-motion
attributes.description: Opt-in (on mv-menu, mv-context-menu or an ancestor): the panel blooms from the corner closest to the trigger (based on data-side / data-align), a single highlight pill glides from item to item (hover and keyboard) instead of per-item backgrounds, and submenus slide out from their row. Without the attribute, rendering is unchanged.

methods.name: hide({ focus })

items.a11y: Section region (implicit role) named “Notifications (Alt+T)”, aria-live=polite (additions and text updates are announced); important:true switches the card to role=alert. The region is created on the first toast (so a server-rendered toaster hydrates cleanly and no empty landmark is listed), and that first toast is inserted 100 ms later, once the screen reader knows the live region; later toasts appear at once. Alt+T moves focus to the latest toast; each card is focusable, Escape dismisses it and focus moves to the next one, then back to the original element. Timers pause on hover, on focus and while the tab is hidden. Animations are reduced automatically (prefers-reduced-motion). Modal dialogs: a modal <dialog> makes the rest of the page inert, top layer included, so while one is open the region moves into the topmost modal <dialog> (opened with showModal(), mv-dialog and its sheets included) and comes back when it closes; toasts stay visible, clickable, swipeable and reachable with Alt+T, after the dialog content in Tab order. Whenever the region moves (into or out of a modal, or with the element moved in the DOM), cards already on screen lose role=alert, so they are not spoken twice; a card shown in the same task as the move (toast() then showModal()) was never announced, so it is rendered again once the region is known; the next toast waits 100 ms, as the first one does. Known limits: a dialog inside a shadow root, or a modal built without <dialog> (aria-modal and a focus trap), is not followed; there, put an mv-toaster inside the modal and target it with the toaster option (toast("Saved", { toaster: "#dialog-toaster" })).

items.a11y: ARIA Tabs pattern: tablist/tab/tabpanel roles, aria-selected, aria-controls and aria-labelledby wired automatically, aria-orientation. Roving tabindex: a single Tab stop to enter the list, arrows (left/right or up/down depending on orientation), Home/End; disabled tabs are skipped. Panels get tabindex=0 and inactive panels are hidden. Reduced motion: instant indicator and fade. Wrapper elements may sit between the host, the tablist, the tabs and the panels (a framework component that renders its own root); a nested mv-tabs, and anything inside a panel, keeps its own tabs. Known limits: panels inside a wrapper are not stacked in one grid cell, so the outgoing panel leaves at once instead of crossfading. Styling wrapped markup relies on CSS @scope (all current engines); without it, only the direct markup (tablist and panels as children of mv-tabs, tabs as children of the tablist) is styled, while wrapped tabs keep working unstyled.

items.a11y:
A group of native
/ disclosures (WAI-ARIA Disclosure pattern, the one the APG uses for FAQs), not the stricter APG Accordion pattern (heading wrapping a button, aria-controls). The browser exposes each as a toggle with its expanded state, kept in sync with open, name and in-page search; Enter and Space toggle, Tab moves between triggers. No arrow keys: they would stop the page from scrolling (removed from the APG accordion pattern in 2026). Put a heading in the trigger (

…

, level chosen for the page) so headings navigation finds each section: NVDA and VoiceOver list it; JAWS and TalkBack may not (2018-2021 tests). Do not add role, aria-expanded or aria-controls to , nor a role to
: the native semantics already carry them, and role="button" hides the heading and the state in Safari. Known limit: with the native marker hidden, some screen readers do not always announce the state change. Closed content is out of the accessibility tree and still findable with Ctrl+F (opens automatically). Reduced motion or no ::details-content: instant open.

items.a11y: Pure CSS on native elements: the document outline, lists, tables and disclosures keep their semantics. Colors come from the tokens (body text and captions at 4.5:1 or more in both themes), links stay underlined, and links, summary, a focusable pre and a focusable table wrapper get a visible focus ring. Give a long <pre> tabindex="0", and wrap a wide table in a plain <div role="region" aria-label="…" tabindex="0"> so keyboard users can scroll it sideways. In forced colors, inline code keeps an outline, keys keep their border and <mark> uses the system Mark colors. No animation. The scoping relies on CSS @scope (all current engines); older browsers show the plain host styles.
